title: Redwood POC - Weekly Sync (Lumina Retail) - Cost/Econ Review
summary: Reviewed POC benchmark numbers for tokens/sec/$ and cache savings.
SE presented optimized batching and KV/prefix caching results — tradeoff: throughput vs tail latency.
Customer asked about expected unit costs at 95% cache hit and for 99th percentile latency impact.
Next steps: Redwood to run 24h load-run with production-like prefix distribution and share updated cost sheet; Lumina to provide representative traffic traces and SSO contact for security review.
next_steps: Tom - run 24h load with Lumina trace and share raw results + updated cost spreadsheet (due 2026-03-06)
Priya - prepare SLO impact note for different batching policies (due 2026-03-09)
Maya - share 48h traffic trace and top 20 prompt templates (due 2026-03-05)
Schedule security deep-dive (Tom to propose times)
action_items: Tom: send updated cost sheet and benchmark csv (due 2026-03-06)
Priya: run additional runs with smaller batches to measure 99th tail (due 2026-03-09)

transcript:
[00:00] Tom: Hey team, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick agenda: results recap, tuning notes, next steps. Uh we'll go about 45 minutes.
[00:18] Maya: Great, thanks Tom. We had a bunch of folks pulled in, Jenna and Aaron are here.
[00:25] Jenna: hi everyone.
[00:30] Tom: Priya from our SE team is presenting the latest cost runs — Priya over to you.
[00:36] Priya: yeah hi — so I ran the two workload profiles you shared: catalog-search and personalized-email. The main axes we measured were tokens/sec, tokens per dollar, and cache hit savings. Quick note, the transcription from our test harness labels some of the model names weird, it shows redwood-gen-2 but that's actually a t5-family fine-tuned variant in the run.
[01:02] Priya: for catalog-search (short prompts, avg seq 48) baseline hosted config (no caching, batching=auto) got ~1,800 tokens/sec across the pool and cost about $0.92 per 1k tokens-equivalent — obviously that's rough because of batching. With prefix/KV cache enabled and 62% hit rate (which matched your sample traffic) effective tokens served dropped by ~38% and cost per effective token dropped to about $0.57 per 1k.
[01:45] Aaron: wait, 0.92 per 1k, then 0.57 after cache? so that's like 38% savings?
[01:53] Priya: yes exactly, those are end-to-end amortized numbers including network + runtime. Our caching model also reduces GPU token compute but still needs some CPU for cache routing.
[02:07] Maya: how did you model batching? we saw in our own infra that bigger batches reduce unit cost but increase tail.
[02:15] Priya: good q — we ran three batching policies: low-latency (batch cap 8), balanced (cap 32), and throughput (cap 128). For the catalog profile: low-latency gave 0.9k tokens/sec/node but 95th latency ~120ms; balanced got 2.2k tokens/sec/node and 95th ~200ms; throughput 128 cap hit 4.6k tokens/sec/node but 95th moved to 450-520ms. So tradeoff is clear — if your SLO is 200ms 95th then balanced is the sweet spot.
[03:10] Tom: we also looked at combined cache+batching — with 62% cache and balanced batching you get the best cost per effective token without blowing 95th too much.
[03:25] Aaron: what about 99th? clients care about p99 for UI flows.
[03:30] Priya: p99 is more sensitive — for the throughput policy we saw p99s spike to 1.1s in some runs. Balanced policy p99 was about 380-420ms depending on burstiness. We can tighten queuing and add priority lanes for low-latency calls, that helps but reduces throughput somewhat.
[03:58] Jenna: can you quantify savings if we hit 80% vs 95% cache?
[04:05] Priya: yes — quick numbers from the matrix: at 62% hit we saw ~38% cost reduction; at 80% hit it's ~52% reduction; at 95% hit it's about ~68% reduction. Those are effective token reductions before considering batching improvements.
[04:30] Maya: those are promising. How realistic is 95% in prod? our catalog has lots of unique product descriptions, maybe 60-70% typical but if we canonicalize prompts we might be able to push to 80.
[04:45] Priya: right canonicalization + light-weight prefixing helps a ton. Also TTL on cache entries and fingerprinting prompt templates matter. We'll share a doc on prompt canonicalization.
[04:59] Tom: I pulled the cost-per-hour math into the sheet (link: https://redwood.app/sheets/lumina-poc-bench). note: link is short-hand in the transcript, actual share in email.
[05:12] Aaron: a question on hardware — are these numbers on A100s or cheaper T4-like cards?
[05:18] Priya: these runs were on dedicated VMs with A10G-equivalent GPU profiles; throughput numbers scale down on T4-class. We have a kernel mix that performs better on Ampere than older gen. We'll annotate the sheet.
[05:33] Maya: ok, want to understand expected unit cost at 99% cache and using balanced batching — what's the per-1M token cost?
[05:41] Priya: rough calc: base compute cost at balanced batching on A10-equivalent is ~$0.60 per 1k tokens before cache; at 95% cache it becomes ~$0.18 per 1k effectively, so per-1M tokens that's about $180. With higher hit it's lower — numbers in sheet.
[06:06] Tom: to confirm, tokens/sec/$ metric — we measured tokens/sec divided by cost-per-second to get tokens per dollar; for catalog balanced policy that's around 3,700 tokens/sec per dollar during steady state, but that depends on batch tail.
[06:25] Aaron: interesting. we run spikes up to 4x during campaign; how does that affect unit cost?
[06:31] Priya: bursts shift you to smaller batches briefly which increases unit cost; but if bursts are short-lived the amortized cost isn't terrible. For sustained 4x load you need autoscale which increases cost linearly. With caching you still save though.
[06:45] Jenna: is there recommendation for autoscale headroom?
[06:48] Priya: we usually recommend 1.5x baseline headroom for headroom, with burst pool for short spikes. Also reserved capacity for predictable load helps with unit economics.
[07:02] Tom: quick dig on measurement: the test harness had slightly higher variance because it used synthetic user think times; we asked Lumina for a real trace which will give better numbers.
[07:12] Maya: yes we'll share the trace today.
[07:16] Aaron: also curious about encryption/KMS cost when using Private — does that add materially?
[07:22] Priya: there's a small compute hit for envelope encryption and calls to KMS are minimal if you use cached keys. The main added cost is management and audit retention. We'll include a security bucket in the sheet.
[07:35] Tom: on competitors — we benchmarked Anthropic on some short prompts, they had lower p95 but cost per token was higher in our runs; Vertex had similar throughput but different pricing model which made reserved capacity less favorable.
[07:50] Maya: ok, good to know.
[07:53] Priya: one more microbenchmark: when we enable prefix caching at the model runtime layer (not just application side) we reduce KV lookup latency and shave about 12-18ms on median. On long prompts that compounds.
[08:10] Jenna: any impact on cold-starts?
[08:13] Priya: cold-starts are mostly unchanged; caching helps once warmed. If you have warm pools you won't notice cold-starts.
[08:20] Tom: let's walk through the recommended pilot config for next week — Priya?
[08:24] Priya: recommended: balanced batching, KV/prefix caching enabled, TTL 24h for entries, reserved pool sized at 1.5x baseline, and a small burst pool. We'll run a 24h test against your real trace to validate cost curve and p95/p99.
[08:40] Maya: sounds good. how do we interpret the cost per conversion? our KPI is conversion per impression.
[08:45] Tom: we can map tokens per interaction to conversion metrics if you share avg tokens per conversion and conv rate; we'll add a conversion tab in the sheet.
[08:54] Aaron: network costs were included?
[08:57] Priya: yes egress and intra-region network included in the amortized model for Hosted; for Private you'll need to model intra-VPC. We'll add a column.
[09:05] Jenna: any ask from our side for security docs?
[09:08] Tom: they want SOC2 and KMS integration docs and SSO flow — I'll attach our security pack.
[09:15] Maya: can we get an estimate for monthly cost at 1M interactions / month, 2M, 5M?
[09:21] Priya: yes we'll prepare those tiers in the sheet; major variable is cache hit and average tokens per interaction.
[09:30] (crosstalk)
[09:40] Priya: note on tuning: increasing batch cap beyond 64 gives diminishing returns if cache hit is high because many requests are served from cache and don't materialize on the GPU. So there's a sweet spot that depends on hit-rate.
[10:00] Tom: let's capture explicit next steps.
[10:05] Maya: quick question — will deduping prompts impact personalization quality?
[10:09] Priya: some care needed; we recommend template-level canonicalization, preserve personalization tokens, and test with your eval set. We'll help with prompts.
[10:20] Jenna: ok thanks.
[10:23] Tom: end recap: Lumina to share trace + prompts; Redwood to run 24h with balanced config and share sheet; schedule security deep dive. We'll reconvene after we have run results. Thanks everyone.
[10:40] Maya: thanks all.
[10:43] meeting end
